description: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the "% point difference" across four different neural network configurations for two models. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled from left to right as "hidden:[50], linear", "hidden:[], linear", "hidden:[100], ReLU", and "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU", with no apparent alphabetical or value-based sorting. The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "% point difference", using a linear scale that ranges from -0.2 to 0.2 with a tick label interval of 0.1. A solid horizontal line marks the 0.0 baseline, and lighter grid lines correspond to the other tick marks. The chart features grouped bars, where each category on the horizontal axis contains a pair of side-by-side bars. According to the legend in the top right corner, the light blue bars represent the "mBERT" model, and the dark blue bars represent the "XLM-R" model. All bars are visually emphasized with thin black outlines. For the "hidden:[50], linear" category, the mBERT bar extends downward to approximately -0.20, representing the lowest negative value in the chart, while the XLM-R bar reaches about -0.06. In the "hidden:[], linear" category, both bars extend upward, with mBERT at roughly 0.09 and XLM-R at approximately 0.21, which is the tallest positive bar shown. For "hidden:[100], ReLU", mBERT is at approximately -0.11 and XLM-R is slightly positive at about 0.02. Finally, in the "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU" category, both bars are negative, with mBERT at roughly -0.18 and XLM-R at approximately -0.14.
